scenarios.title: Triage a suspicious network change
scenarios.summary: Correlate the approved change and the observed behavior, then restore the relay’s management boundary.
scenarios.objective: Use the affected relay’s journal to identify the approved revision, applied revision and post-change restricted-client observation. Record whether the supplied journal establishes a successful sign-in for the same restricted client. Restore access only for the two approved systems and verify the four supplied client trials.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the specific failed trial and compare its actual result with the stated requirement.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A threat is something that could harm the network. A vulnerability is a weakness that could make that possible. An exploit uses a weakness to cause an unauthorized result. Here the broadened management rule is the weakness. The journal and virtual client probes show what was observed.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: Compare the approved revision, the revision that was applied and a later probe on the affected relay. A probe that reaches the sign-in boundary does not establish that the client successfully signed in. Look for a separate sign-in record for that client.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: Restore the approved access boundary. Verify that approved systems still reach the sign-in prompt. Check the restricted clients as well. A broad permit and a blanket block both fail part of the job.

scenarios.explanation: The evidence report ties the approval and the changed revision to the observed restricted client. The repaired policy preserves both allowed clients and restores the two expected denials.
hints: Read device name and minute together. The journal includes entries for a different device.
A reached sign-in prompt is an admission outcome. Only the separate sign-in record describes successful access.
Compare the approved client addresses with the line’s standard source list. Apply an edit before checking the probes.
scenarios.simplifications: Supplied event chronology, evidence selection and virtual routed management admission. A small IOS-style policy subset is used over fixed topology. No real network, credentials, attack activity, logs, authentication or system changes occur. The simulated probe can report the sign-in boundary only.

scenarios.title: Choose a proportionate protection control
scenarios.summary: Set a virtual facility policy that keeps necessary work possible while limiting and recording access to the network room.
scenarios.objective: Keep on-call operator access for the supplied after-hours fault. Allow technician access during staffed hours and allow a registered visitor only with an escort during staffed hours. Keep the denied-event records and route the supplied staff report to the security desk.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the specific failed trial and compare its actual result with the stated requirement.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: Assign permissions for routine work and on-call faults separately. Restrict when maintenance can happen. A full block can stop needed work, while broadly available access exposes the room.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: Registration identifies a visitor in the supplied profile. In the default policy for the example, a visit also needs a present escort and a staffed time window. Check a legitimate visit as well as the failed case.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: An awareness procedure tells staff how to report an unexpected access request. Configure the destination, then inspect whether the supplied report reaches the security desk. Record denied access events for review.

scenarios.explanation: The role, time and escort decisions admit the needed visits and reject the other trials. The policy retains denied-event records and routes the supplied staff report to security.
hints: Separate the on-call operator’s need from planned technician maintenance.
Check the same visitor with and without an escort and at the two supplied times.
The report can reach security directly or through both listed desks.
scenarios.simplifications: Virtual role, time, registration and escort decisions with in-app audit evidence and a local report route. No actual facility, controls, credentials, access tokens, detection service or report delivery is used. The lesson covers the declared policy examples.
